Rules / Correctness

SK2072 The literal contains an unescaped invisible character

A string or character literal holds a zero-width, bidirectional or control character written as itself rather than as an escape sequence.

CategoryCorrectness
Default severitywarning
ScopeSyntax
Needs a compilationno
Runs under --load=looseyes
Cached per fileyes
Fixyes, safe
Language version floor—
Since2.0
SupersedesS2479

Why

A zero-width space, a non-breaking space or a right-to-left override pasted into a literal is invisible in the editor, in the diff and in the review, and it changes what the program does — a key that never matches, a header that never parses, a path that is not the path anybody read. The escape sequence is the same value written so a person can see it, which is why the fix is mechanical and safe. ⚠ Two classes of character, one severity, and that is a decision rather than an oversight. A right-to-left override is the "Trojan Source" class — source that reads as one program and compiles as another — and a stray non-breaking space is a typo. The message says which one it found; the severity does not, because splitting them would spend a second permanent id (ADR-012) to encode a ranking, and a repository that wants the harder line writes dotnet_diagnostic.SK2072.severity = error without needing one.

Example

Instead of:

public const string Tenant = "tenant\u200Bid";   // written with the character itself

Write:

public const string Tenant = "tenant\\u200Bid";  // written as an escape

When it does not fire

⚠ Reported only where an escape is expressible. A verbatim (@"…") or raw ("""…""") literal has no escape sequences at all — that is what those literals are for — and a UTF-8 literal is a separate token kind for the same reason, so all three are silent. ⚠ That is a real hole rather than a tidy boundary: a bidirectional override inside a raw string literal is exactly as dangerous and is not reported, and the honest form of that is to say so rather than to emit a finding with no repair. ⚠ The scan reads the token's source spelling, never its value, which is what makes an already-escaped character silent: in the raw text it is six ASCII characters. Reading the value would report the repair as the problem and the rule would never go quiet. ⚠ Confusable-*width* spaces are deliberately absent from the set — U+2000 to U+200A and U+3000 — because a thin space in typography and an ideographic space in Japanese text are visible, intentional and correct, and reporting them would make the rule an opinion about typesetting. U+00A0 and U+202F stay, because they are indistinguishable from an ordinary space rather than merely narrower than one. Comments and identifiers are not literals and are not scanned; a soft hyphen in an identifier is a naming question that IDE1006 is nearer to. \n and \r are absent from the control set because the language will not carry them: a raw newline in a regular string literal does not compile. The fix always writes \uXXXX and never \xNN, because \x is variable length and consumes greedily — \x9 followed by G is a different character in one case and a compile error in another. Generated code is excluded.
